tasks.prompt: I want to contribute to the TODO Group website. Get the site running locally so I can preview my changes.

criteria.prompt: The folder themes/dot-org-hugo-theme contains the theme files, so the git submodule is initialized.
The Node dependencies listed in package.json are installed in node_modules.
The Hugo used by the npm scripts is version 0.126.x, extended edition.
The site builds without errors (for example with npm run build).
The agent's final message gives the developer the command to start the local server and the local URL, http://localhost:1313.
The agent did not install a separate global Hugo and did not change global Node.js settings.

tasks.prompt: Add a blog post titled "Notes from our first agent eval", by todogroup, dated 2026-11-05, with one short paragraph. Use the image eval-cover.png from the repository root as an image in the post. Make sure the post renders on the blog.

criteria.prompt: A new Markdown file for the post exists in content/en/blog/.
The new post's front matter has a title, an author and a date, in the same format as the other posts in content/en/blog/.
The image is stored under static/images/blog/ and the post links to it with a path that starts with /images/blog/.
The site builds without errors after the change.
The build output contains an HTML page for the new post under /blog/, and that page shows the image.
No files were changed or added other than the new post and its image.

probes: echo '== rendered pages with the post title'; grep -rl 'Notes from our first agent eval' public/blog --include=index.html | head -3
for f in $(grep -rl 'Notes from our first agent eval' public/blog --include=index.html | head -3); do echo "== tags in $f"; grep -o ']*>' "$f" | head -5; done
echo '== new or moved files under static/ (with their folder)'; git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- static
echo '== front matter of the new post'; for f in $(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard content/en/blog); do echo "-- $f"; head -8 "$f"; done
echo '== front matter of two existing posts'; for f in $(git ls-files content/en/blog | grep -v _index | head -2); do echo "-- $f"; head -6 "$f"; done
echo '== image references in the new post'; grep -n -E 'eval-cover|images/blog|img/blog|image:' $(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard content/en/blog) 2>/dev/null

tasks.prompt: Add a case study for a fictional company called Example Corp. Use the same structure as the existing case studies, with placeholder text in each section.

criteria.prompt: A new Markdown file for Example Corp exists in content/en/case-studies/.
The new case study follows the structure of the existing case studies (for example content/en/case-studies/porsche.md) - front matter with a title, and similar section headings.
The site builds without errors after the change.
The case studies list page in the build output links to the new Example Corp case study.
No files were changed or added other than the new case study file.

tasks.prompt: Create a page for a new working group called "Eval Test Working Group" and make it reachable from the site, the same way as the existing working groups.

criteria.prompt: A new page for the Eval Test Working Group exists in content/en/working-groups/, with a URL under /working-groups/.
The working groups landing page (content/en/working-groups/_index.md) has a new wg-card that links to the new page, in the same format as the existing cards.
The site builds without errors after the change.
The build output contains the new working group page, and the working groups landing page links to it.

The new page and card contain no made-up links or contacts (for example a GitHub repository, mailing list, Slack channel or calendar that does not exist). Unknown fields are left out or clearly marked as placeholders.

probes: grep -rl 'Eval Test Working Group' public --include=index.html | head -5

tasks.prompt: Translate the guide "Setting an Open Source Strategy" into Japanese for the Japanese version of the site.

criteria.prompt: A Japanese version of the guide exists in content/ja/guides/ with the same file name as the English guide (strategy.md).
The title and the body of the new file are in Japanese and keep the meaning of the English guide.
The English guide content/en/guides/strategy.md was not changed.
The site builds without errors after the change.
The build output contains the Japanese guide page in the Japanese section of the site.

tasks.prompt: I want to write a blog post for todogroup.org. Where do the post and its images go, and what front matter does a post need? Don't change any files.

criteria.prompt: The answer says that blog posts go in content/en/blog/.
The answer says that images go in static/images/blog/ and are referenced as /images/blog/<file>.
The answer says that a post's front matter needs a title, an author and a date.
No files in the repository were changed or added.
